mutations.label: QY1 THE TICKET: TMPDIR is never exported, so tempfile.mkdtemp() keeps landing in /tmp (the 1.47M entries / 184G that left / with 68M)

QY2 RE-AIMED by #1203r0, whose meaning inverted: this used to mutate the root back onto / and call that the defect. Living on / is now correct (/data measured 20-30x slower for mkdtemp+fsync). The defect is TMPDIR being the BARE SHARED /tmp -- no per-run component, so the tree can never be cleaned without deleting other processes' files.

QY3 a TMPDIR the caller chose is overridden anyway (the #1203qt lesson in reverse: an explicit choice must be left alone). ANCHOR RE-AIMED: the #1203qy fix rewrote this very line ($TMPDIR -> ${TMPDIR:-}) and silently turned QY3 into NOT APPLIED while the suite stayed green -- the patch-destroys-its-own-anchor hazard, inside one session.
QY4 the temp tree is deleted even when the run FAILED, destroying the evidence for the failure
QY5 the un-creatable temp root falls through to /tmp QUIETLY -- the fallback that masks the failure (user's standing rule)
QY6 the naive `$TMPDIR` comes back -- under `set -uo pipefail` that aborts the suite on the UNSET path this block exists to handle (it did, on the first real run)
QY7 basetemp goes back onto the spinning disk -- the half of the temp I/O that #1203qy left behind (573 test files use tmp_path, 300 use mkdtemp)
QY8 THE SWEEP'S SCOPE GUARD is removed, so pointing SUITE_TMPDIR_ROOT at /tmp would delete other processes' temp files
mutations.find: /tmp|/tmp/|/|"") : ;;   # never sweep a shared or empty root
mutations.replace: "@@never@@") : ;;   # never sweep a shared or empty root

mutations.label: QY9 the age gate goes, so a CONCURRENT run's temp tree is deleted underneath it
QY10 the sweep stops naming what it removed (#983: a check that fires naming nothing)
mutations.find: echo "[suite] swept $_swept abandoned temp tree(s) older than ${SUITE_TMP_KEEP_DAYS:-3}d from $_sweep_root"
